classification.difficultyReason: Apply rationality definitions to roots, multiples and recurring decimals, then use calculator values to round and position each number on supplied labelled lines, including a negative root. Explicit table headings and the partly completed e row scaffold these direct taught procedures.

answer.worked: $e\approx2.72$. Mark the point about $0.72$ of the way from $2$ to $3$.

spec.description: Completed number line with a point at e.

answer.worked: $\sqrt{6}=2.449489742\ldots$. It is non-terminating and non-recurring, so it is irrational. To 2 d.p., $\sqrt{6}\approx2.45$; to 3 d.p., $\sqrt{6}\approx2.449$. Mark between $2$ and $3$, just left of the midpoint.
$2\sqrt{6}=4.898979486\ldots$, which is non-terminating and non-recurring, so it is irrational. To 2 d.p., $2\sqrt{6}\approx4.90$; to 3 d.p., $2\sqrt{6}\approx4.899$. Mark just left of $5$.

$\sqrt{24}=4.898979486\ldots$, which is non-terminating and non-recurring, so it is irrational. To 2 d.p., $\sqrt{24}\approx4.90$; to 3 d.p., $\sqrt{24}\approx4.899$. Mark just left of $5$, at the same location as $2\sqrt{6}$.

$\sqrt{13}=3.605551275\ldots$, which is non-terminating and non-recurring, so it is irrational. To 2 d.p., $\sqrt{13}\approx3.61$; to 3 d.p., $\sqrt{13}\approx3.606$. Mark between $3$ and $4$, about $0.61$ of the way from $3$.
$\sqrt{16}=4=\frac{4}{1}$, so it is rational. Written to 2 d.p. it is $4.00$; to 3 d.p. it is $4.000$. Mark exactly at $4$.
$\pi=3.141592654\ldots$ is non-terminating and non-recurring, so it is irrational. To 2 d.p., $\pi\approx3.14$; to 3 d.p., $\pi\approx3.142$. Mark just right of $3$.

$3\pi=9.424777961\ldots$, which is non-terminating and non-recurring, so it is irrational. To 2 d.p., $3\pi\approx9.42$; to 3 d.p., $3\pi\approx9.425$. Mark between $9$ and $10$, just left of the midpoint.

answer.short: Rational; $0.33$ (2 d.p.), $0.333$ (3 d.p.). Mark at about $0.33$.
answer.worked: $0.\dot{3}=0.333333\ldots=\frac13$. The decimal recurs, so it is rational. To 2 d.p. it is $0.33$; to 3 d.p. it is $0.333$. Mark one-third of the way from $0$ to $1$.

answer.short: Rational; $2.33$ (2 d.p.), $2.333$ (3 d.p.). Mark at about $2.33$.
answer.worked: $\frac73=2.333333\ldots$. It is a fraction of integers with a nonzero denominator, so it is rational. To 2 d.p. it is $2.33$; to 3 d.p. it is $2.333$. Mark one-third of the way from $2$ to $3$.
$-5=\frac{-5}{1}$, so it is rational. Written to 2 d.p. it is $-5.00$; to 3 d.p. it is $-5.000$. Mark exactly at $-5$.

$-\sqrt{3}=-1.732050808\ldots$, which is non-terminating and non-recurring, so it is irrational. To 2 d.p., $-\sqrt{3}\approx-1.73$; to 3 d.p., $-\sqrt{3}\approx-1.732$. Mark between $-2$ and $-1$, closer to $-2$.
